models.name: costly_bounded_alternatives_listener
models.rationale: Bounded alternatives listener with utterance production costs (depth 1). Refinement of bounded_alternatives_listener: speakers trade off communicative informativeness against utterance production costs, penalizing non-distinctive words that apply to multiple referents. Resource-limited listeners invert this cost-sensitive speaker with bounded attention that discounts unmentioned alternative expressions relative to the focal heard word.

models.name: graded_specificity_listener
models.rationale: Graded specificity listener: referent choice driven by graded descriptive truth values.

models.name: bounded_alternatives_listener
models.rationale: Bounded alternatives listener: resource-limited listener with limited attention to alternative utterances. Listeners have bounded attentional resources to generate and reason over unmentioned alternative utterances when interpreting a speaker. When simulating the speaker's utterance choice, a resource-limited listener discounts unmentioned alternative expressions relative to the focal heard word, reducing the speaker's perceived likelihood of having chosen an alternative descriptor. Under limited attention to alternatives, the listener relies predominantly on literal semantics and contextual salience, attenuating the pragmatic pressure of scalar implicature.

models.name: parsimonious_literal_mixture (exported)
models.rationale: Parsimonious literal mixture: population mixture of literal and parsimonious listeners.

models.name: rsa_l1_shared_prior (seed)
models.rationale: RSA pragmatic listener (depth 1) with a salience prior at every level. As the salience model, but the prior over objects is common knowledge: the literal listener the speaker simulates uses it too (the paper's "mutual knowledge" variant), so salience shapes which word a speaker would choose as well as the listener's inference. Salience is a softmax of w_features per feature an object has plus w_familiar times its familiarization base rate. With no informative word the choice is that prior. A lapse parameter mixes in uniform guessing.

metric.lede: How well each model predicts which referent people pick in the held-out conditions: conditions of the same papers that the loop never saw. Every model was fitted to the loop's training trials only. The panels show people's choice proportions against the models' predictions for each held-out game, word and condition.
metric.standing_note: Held-out log predictive density behind the best of these models, in nats (whiskers ±2 SE of the difference, clustered by held-out condition). Lower is better. r and RMSE compare predicted and observed choice proportions over held-out display cells.
